stimuli.title: नीचे दिए गए गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
stimuli.text:
गाँव के बीचोंबीच एक पुराना तालाब था। बरसों पहले उसी के पानी से खेत सींचे जाते थे और पशु अपनी प्यास बुझाते थे, पर धीरे-धीरे लोग उसमें कूड़ा फेंकने लगे। पानी काला पड़ गया और किनारों पर बदबू फैलने लगी।

एक दिन प्राथमिक विद्यालय की कक्षा पाँच के बच्चों ने अपनी शिक्षिका के साथ तालाब का सर्वेक्षण किया। उन्होंने एक सप्ताह तक गिना कि रोज़ कितने लोग वहाँ कचरा डालते हैं और यह गिनती एक चार्ट पर लिखकर ग्राम सभा की बैठक में रख दी। बच्चों की बात सुनकर बड़ों को शर्म भी आई और प्रेरणा भी मिली।

अगले महीने पूरे गाँव ने मिलकर तालाब की सफ़ाई की, किनारों पर पेड़ लगाए और कूड़े के लिए अलग गड्ढा बनाया। आज उस तालाब में फिर से कमल खिलते हैं। गाँव की बूढ़ी दादी कहती हैं, "जिस बात को हम बड़े भूल गए थे, वह बच्चों ने याद दिला दी।"

stimuli.title: नीचे दिए गए गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
stimuli.text:
रामदीन कुम्हार हर साल दीपावली से पहले हज़ारों दीये बनाता था। चाक पर घूमती मिट्टी उसके हाथों में ऐसे ढलती थी, मानो वह कोई जादू जानता हो। पिछले कुछ वर्षों से बाज़ार में बिजली की रंगीन लड़ियाँ भर गई थीं और दीयों की माँग घट गई थी। रामदीन का पोता सोनू सोचता था कि दादा जी का हुनर अब किसी काम का नहीं रहा।

इस बार विद्यालय में 'स्थानीय हुनर' पर एक प्रदर्शनी लगी। सोनू दादा जी को साथ ले गया। बच्चों ने पहली बार चाक को घूमते और गीली मिट्टी को दीये में बदलते देखा। कई बच्चों ने खुद दीया बनाने की कोशिश की और मिट्टी से सने हाथ लेकर खूब हँसे।

प्रदर्शनी के बाद अनेक परिवारों ने रामदीन से दीये मँगवाए। सोनू समझ गया कि हुनर कभी पुराना नहीं होता, बस उसे पहचानने वाली आँखें चाहिए।

stimuli.title: नीचे दिए गए गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
stimuli.text:
हमारे मोहल्ले के कोने में एक बूढ़ा नीम का पेड़ है। गर्मियों की दोपहर में जब सड़कें तपने लगती हैं, तब उसकी घनी छाया में रिक्शेवाले सुस्ताते हैं, बच्चे गिल्ली-डंडा खेलते हैं और सब्ज़ी बेचने वाली अम्मा अपनी टोकरी उतारती हैं।

पिछले साल नगर निगम ने सड़क चौड़ी करने के लिए उस पेड़ को काटने का निर्णय लिया। मोहल्ले के लोग अधिकारियों से मिले और नक्शा दोबारा देखने का अनुरोध किया। जाँच में पता चला कि सड़क को थोड़ा-सा मोड़ देने से पेड़ बच सकता है।

आज नीम वहीं खड़ा है और उसके नीचे एक छोटा चबूतरा भी बन गया है, जहाँ शाम को बुज़ुर्ग बैठकर बातें करते हैं।

stimuli.title: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.
stimuli.text:
When Kamla Devi turned sixty, she decided she had waited long enough. For years she had pressed her thumb on papers she could not read, trusting others to tell her what they said. One winter evening she joined the literacy class that met on the school verandah after dark. The other learners were two farmers, a tailor and a young mother who brought her baby.

At first Kamla's fingers shook so much that her letters wandered off the line. Her teacher, a college student named Ritu, never corrected her in front of the others. She simply wrote the word again, slowly, beside Kamla's attempt, and waited.

By spring Kamla could read the boards on the buses and the labels on her medicine bottles. The day she signed her name at the bank, the clerk looked up in surprise. Kamla smiled and said nothing. Some victories, she thought, are too large for words.

stimuli.title: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.
stimuli.text:
Every morning the first passenger train brought the newspapers to Sarai Junction, and every morning Bablu was waiting on the platform. He was eleven and sold tea in small clay cups from his uncle's stall, but his real job, as he saw it, was to read the front page before anyone else did. He read slowly, moving his lips, while the kettle hissed behind him.

Travellers sometimes laughed at the tea boy with a newspaper, but the old stationmaster did not. He began to leave the previous day's paper on the bench for Bablu, folded open at the puzzle page. Neither of them ever mentioned it.

Months later, when a new school opened two kilometres away, it was the stationmaster who walked over to speak to Bablu's uncle. "A boy who reads before breakfast," he said, "should not spend his life counting cups."

stimuli.title: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.
stimuli.text: In a narrow lane behind the market, old Rahim made kites from tissue paper and thin strips of bamboo. Every evening children crowded around his door to watch his quick, patient hands. When a boy complained that his kite kept falling, Rahim did not take it from him. He asked the boy to feel which way the wind was blowing, then turned him round to face it. "A kite does not climb with the wind," he said. "It climbs against it." The boy tried again, and this time the kite rose until it was only a red dot above the rooftops.

questions.stem: Spearman explained intelligence as one general ability (g) plus separate specific abilities (s). This is his
questions.explanation: Charles Spearman's two-factor theory has a general factor running through all mental work and specific factors for particular tasks. Multiple intelligences is Gardner's theory and the triarchic theory is Sternberg's.

questions.stem: A child looks only at how tall a glass is and ignores how wide it is. Piaget called this narrow focus on one feature
questions.explanation: Centration, attending to one striking feature and ignoring the others, is a limit of preoperational thinking. Seriation is putting things in order, and accommodation is changing a scheme to fit new experience.

questions.stem: A girl shares her tiffin mainly so that her teacher will see her as a good girl. In Kohlberg's theory, this reasoning fits the stage of
questions.explanation: At Kohlberg's stage 3 (the first stage of the conventional level) children act to win approval and be seen as nice. Punishment and obedience is stage 1, law and order stage 4, and social contract stage 5.

questions.stem: A girl aged 8 has a mental age of 10. What is her intelligence quotient (ratio IQ)?
questions.explanation: Ratio IQ = mental age / chronological age x 100 = 10 / 8 x 100 = 125. Dividing the other way round, 8 / 10 x 100, gives 80.

questions.stem: A Class 4 child has low vision. Which step helps her most in the classroom?
options: Large print and a seat near the board
Copying notes from a classmate later
A seat at the back so she is not noticed
questions.explanation: Children with low vision need materials they can see (large print, good light, high contrast) and a seat close to the board. Excusing them from reading or hiding them at the back shuts them out of learning.

questions.stem: A Class 3 girl understands lessons well but is very clumsy: she struggles to use scissors, tie laces or copy shapes. This suggests
questions.explanation: Dyspraxia is a difficulty in planning and coordinating movement, seen in fine motor tasks such as cutting and tying. Dyslexia affects reading and dyscalculia number sense.

questions.stem: A teacher has children recite a times table every day so that the bond between question and answer grows stronger. This applies Thorndike's
questions.explanation: Thorndike's law of exercise says connections are strengthened by use and weakened by disuse, which is the reason for regular practice. The law of effect is about satisfying results.

questions.stem: A child bitten by one dog now feels afraid on seeing any dog. In classical conditioning, this spread of the response is called
questions.explanation: When a conditioned response is set off by stimuli similar to the original one, it has generalised. Discrimination is the opposite: responding only to the original stimulus.

questions.stem: A child starts greeting visitors with folded hands after watching her elder brother do it. This is
questions.explanation: Bandura's social learning theory shows that children learn by watching and imitating models. No reward or bell is needed for the child to pick up the behaviour.

questions.stem: Section 17 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 prohibits
options: examinations of every kind in primary school
homework for children in Classes 1 and 2
teaching in the child's home language
questions.explanation: Section 17 of the RTE Act says no child shall be subjected to physical punishment or mental harassment. The Act does not ban homework or the home language.

questions.stem: A teacher gives a short test to find exactly which steps of division a child gets wrong. This is a
questions.explanation: A diagnostic test locates the specific difficulty so the teacher can plan remedial teaching. A summative test sums up learning at the end of a unit or term.

questions.stem: Thorndike's hungry cat escaped from a puzzle box faster and faster over many attempts. This showed learning by
questions.explanation: The cat made many random moves until one opened the box, and the successful move was gradually stamped in. Insight learning, by contrast, comes as a sudden grasp of the whole problem.

questions.stem: तालाब का पानी काला क्यों पड़ गया था?
options: उसमें गाँव के पशु नहाने लगे थे
किनारों के सारे पेड़ कट गए थे
लोग उसमें कूड़ा फेंकने लगे थे
बरसात बहुत कम होने लगी थी
questions.explanation: The passage says धीरे-धीरे लोग उसमें कूड़ा फेंकने लगे, and then the water turned black. Animals drinking from it is mentioned only as its old use.

questions.stem: बच्चों ने ग्राम सभा की बैठक में क्या रखा?
options: लगाए जाने वाले पेड़ों की सूची
questions.explanation: For a week the children counted how many people dumped rubbish, wrote the count on a chart and put it before the gram sabha.

questions.stem: गद्यांश के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त शीर्षक कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: The passage is about children whose survey made the whole village act. The lotus and the grandmother are details near the end, not the main idea.

questions.stem: गद्यांश में आए शब्द "बदबू" का विलोम शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: बदबू means a bad smell, so its opposite is सुगंध (a pleasant smell). दुर्गंध is a synonym of बदबू, not its opposite.

questions.stem: "च, छ, ज, झ" वर्णों का उच्चारण स्थान क्या है?
questions.explanation: The च-वर्ग is spoken with the tongue against the palate (तालु), so these are तालव्य वर्ण. The क-वर्ग is कंठ्य, the ट-वर्ग मूर्धन्य and the त-वर्ग दंत्य.

questions.stem: "महोत्सव" शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
questions.explanation: महा + उत्सव: आ + उ = ओ, which is गुण संधि.

questions.stem: "चंद्रमुख" में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation: चंद्रमुख = चंद्र के समान मुख. The face is compared with the moon (उपमान and उपमेय), so it is कर्मधारय समास. द्विगु needs a number word as the first part.

questions.stem: "सुख-दुख" शब्द के बीच लगे छोटे चिह्न (-) को क्या कहते हैं?
questions.explanation: The short hyphen that joins the two words of a pair is the योजक चिह्न. The निर्देशक चिह्न is a longer dash used to introduce or explain.

questions.stem: कक्षा 1 में वर्णों की पहचान कराने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त सामग्री कौन-सी है?
questions.explanation: Picture-letter cards (अ से अनार) link each letter to a familiar object and sound, which suits a Class 1 child. Grammar books, dictionaries and essay books are for much later.

questions.stem: "देखो और कहो" विधि से पढ़ना सिखाते समय बच्चे पहले क्या पहचानते हैं?
options: पूरे शब्द को चित्र के साथ
questions.explanation: The look-and-say method starts from whole words shown with pictures, which children recognise by their shape and meaning. Building words from letter sounds is the phonic (ध्वनि) method.

questions.stem: श्रुतलेख (बोलकर लिखवाना) से मुख्य रूप से किस बात की जाँच होती है?
options: मौलिक विचार अपने शब्दों में लिखने की
सुनकर शुद्ध वर्तनी में लिखने की
questions.explanation: In श्रुतलेख the teacher speaks and the child writes, so it checks listening and spelling (वर्तनी) together. Original expression is checked through रचनात्मक लेखन.

questions.stem: कक्षा 2 के बच्चों का सुलेख सुधारने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त उपाय क्या है?
options: वर्णों की सही बनावट का अभ्यास
questions.explanation: Good handwriting grows from practising the correct shape, size and stroke order of each letter. Fast copying and pages of writing tire children and fix bad habits.

questions.stem: Why did Kamla Devi join the literacy class?
options: She was tired of relying on others to read
She wanted to become a teacher like Ritu one day
Her bank told her she must learn to read
Her grandchildren asked her to join
questions.explanation: She had pressed her thumb on papers she could not read, trusting others to tell her what they said, and 'decided she had waited long enough'. The bank appears only at the end.

questions.stem: How did Ritu help Kamla with her writing?
options: By guiding her hand on the page
By correcting her in front of the class
By giving her extra homework each night
By writing the word again beside hers
questions.explanation: Ritu 'never corrected her in front of the others' but 'wrote the word again, slowly, beside Kamla's attempt, and waited'.

questions.stem: The phrase 'her letters wandered off the line' suggests that her writing was
questions.explanation: Letters that wander off the line are uneven, because her fingers shook. Nothing in the passage mentions their size or what she wrote with.

questions.stem: What does Kamla mean by 'Some victories are too large for words'?
options: She thought winning was not important
She did not want the clerk to know
She felt more than she could express
She still could not read long words
questions.explanation: Signing her name was so big a moment for her that no words could hold the feeling, so she simply smiled. The line is about emotion, not about her reading level.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: "The goat jumped ___ the low wall into the field."
questions.explanation: 'Over' shows movement from one side of something to the other by going above it. 'Above' only describes position, not movement across.

questions.stem: Choose the correct article: "___ European tourist asked us the way to the fort."
questions.explanation: 'European' begins with a 'yoo' sound, a consonant sound, so it takes 'a' even though it is spelt with a vowel. The choice depends on sound, not spelling.

questions.stem: Which word is opposite in meaning to 'humble'?
questions.explanation: 'Humble' means modest, not thinking oneself better than others, so its opposite is 'proud'. 'Simple' and 'gentle' are close in feeling to humble.

questions.stem: Change into the passive voice: "The children planted the saplings."
options: The children were planted by the saplings.
The saplings were planted by the children.
The saplings are planted by the children.
The saplings had been planted by children.
questions.explanation: The simple past active 'planted' becomes 'were planted' in the passive, with the object 'the saplings' as the new subject. The tense must stay simple past.

questions.stem: The audio-lingual method of teaching English relies mainly on
questions.explanation: The audio-lingual method, based on behaviourism, has learners repeat and drill model sentences until correct patterns become habits.

questions.stem: Which method of teaching English relies mainly on translating into and out of the mother tongue?
questions.explanation: The grammar-translation method teaches rules and translates sentences between the two languages. The direct method avoids the mother tongue altogether.

questions.stem: Which activity best builds phonemic awareness in Class 1?
options: Finding words that begin with the same sound
Learning the spellings of ten new words
Copying a long paragraph neatly from the board
questions.explanation: Phonemic awareness is the ability to hear and play with the separate sounds in words. Matching words by their first sound trains exactly that; copying and spelling lists do not.

questions.stem: The communicative approach to teaching English puts most weight on
options: learning long lists of word meanings
questions.explanation: The communicative approach treats language as a tool for doing things: asking, telling, persuading. Accuracy matters, but fluency in meaningful use comes first.

questions.stem: What is the difference between the place value and the face value of 6 in 3,62,859?
questions.explanation: The 6 is in the ten thousands place, so its place value is 60,000 and its face value is 6: 60,000 - 6 = 59,994. Adding them gives 60,006.

questions.stem: Which Roman numeral stands for 94?
questions.explanation: 94 = 90 + 4 = XC + IV = XCIV. XCVI is 96, and LXL and IVXC are not valid Roman numerals.

questions.stem: Which fraction is equivalent to 18/24?
questions.explanation: Divide the numerator and the denominator by their HCF, 6: 18/24 = 3/4. Check by cross-multiplying: 18 x 4 = 72 = 24 x 3. 2/3, 3/5 and 9/16 all fail that check.
Line up the decimal points: 2.50 + 0.75 + 3.05 = 6.30, which is 6.3. Writing 2.5 as 2.05 by mistake gives 5.85.

questions.stem: How many edges does a pyramid with a square base have?
questions.explanation: The square base has 4 edges and 4 more run from its corners up to the apex: 4 + 4 = 8. The pyramid has 5 faces and 5 vertices; 12 is the number of edges of a cube.

questions.stem: 3 km 45 m is equal to
questions.explanation: 1 km = 1000 m, so 3 km 45 m = 3000 + 45 = 3045 m. 45 m sits in the tens and ones places, not the hundreds.

questions.stem: A train leaves Lucknow at 21:40 and reaches its destination at 05:15 the next morning. How long is the journey?
questions.explanation: From 21:40 to midnight is 2 h 20 min, and from midnight to 05:15 is 5 h 15 min: 7 h 35 min in all. Subtracting 05:15 from 21:40 gives 16 h 25 min, the wrong way round.

questions.stem: 7 pens cost Rs 91. How many rupees do 4 such pens cost? Type the number only.
questions.explanation: One pen costs 91 / 7 = Rs 13, so 4 pens cost 13 x 4 = Rs 52.

questions.stem: The inductive method of teaching mathematics moves from
options: a general rule to specific examples
specific examples to a general rule
questions.explanation: In the inductive method children work through several examples and discover the rule, for example noticing that the angles of many triangles add up to 180 degrees. The deductive method starts with the rule.

questions.stem: A child works out 23 x 14 as 92 + 23 = 115. What does the child most need help with?
options: Place value of the tens digit
questions.explanation: 23 x 4 = 92 is right, but 23 x 1 ten should be written as 230, not 23. The child has forgotten that the 1 in 14 stands for a ten: 92 + 230 = 322.

questions.stem: An abacus is most useful for teaching
questions.explanation: Each rod of an abacus stands for a place (ones, tens, hundreds), so children see that the same bead means different values on different rods.

questions.stem: Children use the seven pieces of a tangram to make animals and other shapes. This mainly develops
questions.explanation: Fitting tangram pieces together builds a feel for how shapes combine, turn and flip, an early part of geometry.

questions.stem: Which tree is the state tree of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Ashoka (Saraca asoca) is Uttar Pradesh's state tree. The banyan is India's national tree.

questions.stem: A cactus stores water mainly in its
questions.explanation: A cactus has a thick, fleshy green stem that stores water and makes food. Its leaves have become spines, which cut down water loss.

questions.stem: Cows, goats and camels bring swallowed food back to the mouth and chew it again. Such animals are called
questions.explanation: Animals that chew the cud are ruminants; their stomach has several parts. Rodents such as rats gnaw with ever-growing front teeth.

questions.stem: How many milk teeth does a child usually have?
questions.explanation: Children have 20 milk teeth, which fall out from about age 6 and are replaced by permanent teeth. An adult usually has 32.

questions.stem: Which of these foods is a good source of iron?
questions.explanation: Green leafy vegetables such as spinach, along with jaggery and pulses, provide iron, which is needed for healthy blood. Rice is mainly carbohydrate.

questions.stem: Rekha stirs a little alum (phitkari) into muddy pond water and leaves it to stand. The alum mainly
options: makes the mud settle to the bottom
kills every germ in the water
questions.explanation: Alum makes the tiny mud particles clump together so they sink and the clear water can be poured off (loading, then decantation). It does not make the water safe to drink; that still needs boiling or proper filtering.

questions.stem: On a map, what does blue colour usually show?
questions.explanation: Maps use blue for rivers, lakes and seas, green for plains, and brown for hills and mountains.

questions.stem: The Taj Mahal at Agra stands on the bank of which river?
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal is on the south bank of the Yamuna at Agra. Lucknow lies on the Gomti.

questions.stem: Under NCF 2005, how is environmental studies handled in Classes 1 and 2?
options: As a separate social science subject
questions.explanation: NCF 2005 recommends no separate EVS textbook in Classes 1 and 2: environmental themes are integrated into language and mathematics. EVS becomes a subject of its own from Class 3.

questions.stem: Class 4 children ask their families where their drinking water comes from and record the answers in a table. This is the
questions.explanation: Collecting information from people through questions and recording it is a survey. It links EVS with the child's own home and community.

questions.stem: A teacher draws 'Water' in the centre of the board and children add connected ideas around it. This is a
questions.explanation: A concept map shows how ideas link to a central theme. It helps children organise what they know and reveals what they do not.

questions.stem: A child draws and labels a bean seed each day for ten days as it sprouts. Which EVS indicator does this mainly assess?
questions.explanation: Watching a change over days and putting it down in drawings and labels is observation and recording, one of the EVS assessment indicators in NCERT's source book.

questions.stem: The years from about 6 to 12, when children form groups and gangs with friends of the same age, are called
questions.explanation: Later childhood, the primary school years, is often called the gang age because peer groups become so important. Early childhood is roughly 2 to 6 years and adolescence begins around 12.

questions.stem: Which of Piaget's stages covers roughly the first two years of life?
questions.explanation: In the sensorimotor stage, from birth to about 2 years, infants learn through their senses and movements, and develop object permanence.

questions.stem: Vygotsky held that a skill first appears between people and only later inside the child. For him, learning is therefore mainly
questions.explanation: Vygotsky's sociocultural theory says higher mental functions start in social interaction with adults and peers and are then internalised by the child.

questions.stem: A Class 3 child regularly says 'tat' for 'cat' and 'wabbit' for 'rabbit'. This is most likely
questions.explanation: Swapping or distorting particular speech sounds well past the usual age is an articulation (speech sound) disorder. Stammering is a break in the flow of speech.

questions.stem: In Classes 3 to 5, children increasingly take their ideas about dress, games and slang from
questions.explanation: In later childhood the peer group becomes a strong agent of socialisation alongside the family. Children copy friends' games, language and ideas of what is fashionable.

questions.stem: A child easily tells apart birds, leaves and insects and loves sorting them. In Gardner's theory, this shows strong
questions.explanation: Gardner added naturalist intelligence for skill in recognising and classifying living things and features of nature. Spatial intelligence is about picturing shapes and space.

questions.stem: A child is let off cleaning duty whenever she finishes her work on time, and she finishes on time more often. This is
questions.explanation: Removing something unpleasant (cleaning duty) to strengthen a behaviour is negative reinforcement. It is not punishment, because the behaviour increases.

questions.stem: A stage in learning a skill when progress seems to stop for a while is called a
questions.explanation: On a learning curve, a flat stretch where little improvement shows is a plateau. It often comes before a new rise once the learner reorganises the skill.

questions.stem: A child used to writing Hindi from left to right at first finds Urdu, written right to left, confusing. This is
questions.explanation: When earlier learning gets in the way of new learning, transfer is negative. Positive transfer would make the new task easier.

questions.stem: Bloom and his colleagues divided educational objectives into the cognitive, the affective and the
questions.explanation: The three domains are cognitive (knowing), affective (feelings and attitudes) and psychomotor (physical skills).

questions.stem: Under the Schedule to the RTE Act, what should the pupil-teacher ratio be in a primary school?
questions.explanation: The RTE Schedule sets norms of 30 pupils per teacher at the primary level (Classes 1 to 5) and 35 at the upper primary level.

questions.stem: A test at the end of the term that decides each child's grade is an example of
questions.explanation: Summative assessment sums up what was learned at the end of a period. Formative assessment happens during learning to guide the next step of teaching.

questions.stem: दीयों की माँग क्यों घट गई थी?
options: मिट्टी बहुत महँगी हो गई थी
लोगों ने दीपावली मनाना छोड़ दिया था
बिजली की लड़ियाँ आ गई थीं
questions.explanation: The passage says the market had filled with coloured electric lights, so fewer people bought clay lamps.

questions.stem: "मिट्टी उसके हाथों में ऐसे ढलती थी, मानो वह कोई जादू जानता हो" में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.explanation: मानो signals that one thing is imagined to be another (a possibility, not a comparison), which is उत्प्रेक्षा अलंकार. उपमा uses words such as सा, सम or जैसा to compare.

questions.stem: प्रदर्शनी के बाद सोनू ने क्या समझा?
options: बिजली की लड़ियाँ ही अच्छी हैं
questions.explanation: The last line says सोनू समझ गया कि हुनर कभी पुराना नहीं होता, बस उसे पहचानने वाली आँखें चाहिए.

questions.stem: गद्यांश में आया शब्द "कुम्हार" किस तत्सम शब्द का तद्भव रूप है?
questions.explanation: कुंभ (pot) + कार (maker) = कुंभकार, which became कुम्हार. कुंभीर means a crocodile, and कर्मकार means a worker.

questions.stem: हिंदी वर्णमाला में "अं" और "अः" को क्या कहा जाता है?
questions.explanation: अनुस्वार (अं) and विसर्ग (अः) are neither true vowels nor true consonants, so they are called अयोगवाह. य, र, ल, व are अंतःस्थ and श, ष, स, ह are ऊष्म.

questions.stem: "सुबरन को खोजत फिरत कवि, व्यभिचारी, चोर" में "सुबरन" शब्द के कारण कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.explanation: सुबरन is used once but carries three meanings at the same time: good words for the poet, beauty for the lover and gold for the thief. One word with several meanings is श्लेष; यमक needs the same word repeated with different meanings.

questions.stem: "आँख" का पर्यायवाची शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: नयन, लोचन and नेत्र all mean the eye. नभ is the sky, नीर is water and नृप is a king.

questions.stem: "दही" शब्द का लिंग क्या है?
questions.explanation: Standard Hindi says दही खट्टा है, so दही is पुल्लिंग even though it ends in ई. Hindi has no नपुंसकलिंग; that gender belongs to Sanskrit.

questions.stem: व्याकरण शिक्षण की आगमन विधि में शिक्षक किस क्रम में चलता है?
questions.explanation: In the inductive (आगमन) method children study several examples and then find the rule themselves. The निगमन method gives the rule first and then examples.

questions.stem: प्राथमिक कक्षाओं में कविता शिक्षण का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है?
questions.explanation: At the primary stage a poem is taught so that children enjoy its rhythm, feeling and imagery. Memorising meanings or the poet's life turns the poem into a chore.

questions.stem: कक्षा 3 का एक बच्चा "श" को "स" बोलता है। शिक्षक के लिए सबसे उचित उपाय क्या है?
options: पूरी कक्षा के सामने बार-बार टोकना
उसे बोलने के अवसर कम देना
questions.explanation: Pronunciation improves when the child hears the correct sound often and practises it in a relaxed setting. Correcting in front of the class or giving fewer chances to speak only makes the child hesitant.

questions.stem: कक्षा में बाल पत्रिकाएँ और कहानी की किताबें रखने का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है?
questions.explanation: A class library of children's magazines and story books gives children something they want to read, which builds the reading habit. It adds to the textbook rather than replacing it.

questions.stem: What did Bablu think of as his real job?
options: Selling tea in small clay cups
questions.explanation: He sold tea, 'but his real job, as he saw it, was to read the front page before anyone else did'.

questions.stem: Why did the stationmaster leave the previous day's paper on the bench?
options: Because Bablu had asked for it
Because he had finished with it
questions.explanation: Unlike the travellers who laughed, the stationmaster quietly fed Bablu's love of reading, even folding the paper open at the puzzle page for him.

questions.stem: The line 'Neither of them ever mentioned it' shows that the stationmaster's help was
questions.explanation: The help was given and accepted without words, which shows a quiet, unspoken kindness rather than a deal or an official duty.

questions.stem: As used in the passage, 'previous' means
questions.explanation: 'The previous day's paper' is the paper from the day before, so 'previous' means earlier. 'Latest' is nearly its opposite.

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: "By the time we reached the hall, the programme ___."
questions.explanation: The programme started before we reached, an earlier action in the past, so the past perfect 'had begun' is needed.

questions.stem: Which word is closest in meaning to 'frail'?
questions.explanation: 'Frail' means weak and delicate, often used of old or sick people.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: Meena said, "I am writing a letter."
options: Meena said that she was writing a letter.
Meena said that I am writing a letter.
Meena said that she is writing a letter.
Meena told that she was writing a letter.
questions.explanation: With the reporting verb in the past, the present continuous 'am writing' becomes the past continuous 'was writing', and 'I' becomes 'she'. 'Told' needs an object (told us), so 'Meena told that' is wrong.

questions.stem: Which word is spelt correctly?
questions.explanation: Miniature keeps the 'a' of its Italian root after 'mini': m-i-n-i-a-t-u-r-e. It is often misspelt because the 'a' is barely heard.

questions.stem: A teacher has children practise pairs such as 'ship' and 'sheep', 'bit' and 'beat'. This is a
questions.explanation: Minimal pairs differ in a single sound, so practising them helps children hear and say sounds that their home language may not separate.

questions.stem: Reading many easy books for pleasure, without stopping to study each word, is called
questions.explanation: Extensive reading means reading a lot, for meaning and enjoyment. Intensive reading studies a short text closely for language and detail.

questions.stem: Using rhymes and action songs in a Class 1 English class mainly helps children
options: learn the rules of English grammar
enjoy English and hear its sounds
questions.explanation: Rhymes and songs give young children repeated, enjoyable exposure to the sounds and rhythm of English and build confidence before formal reading.

questions.stem: A teacher shares a simple rubric with children before they write a letter. This mainly helps them
options: know what good work looks like
compete with each other for the top mark
questions.explanation: A rubric makes the criteria for a good letter clear in advance, so children can aim at them and check their own drafts.

questions.stem: What is the successor of the largest 6-digit number?
questions.explanation: The largest 6-digit number is 9,99,999, and its successor is one more: 10,00,000 (ten lakh). 9,99,998 is its predecessor, and 1,00,000 is the smallest 6-digit number.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers is divisible by 9?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 9 when its digit sum is: 6 + 3 + 7 + 2 = 18. 6375 has digit sum 21, so it is divisible by 3 but not by 9.

questions.stem: How many prime numbers are there between 60 and 80?
questions.explanation: The primes are 61, 67, 71, 73 and 79: five of them. 63, 69 and 77 look prime but are 7 x 9, 3 x 23 and 7 x 11; counting them too gives 6, 7 or 8.

questions.stem: Ramesh spends 3/8 of his pocket money on books and 1/4 on snacks. What fraction is left?
questions.explanation: 3/8 + 1/4 = 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8 is spent, so 1 - 5/8 = 3/8 is left. 5/8 is the part spent, not the part left.

questions.stem: The perimeter of a square field is 52 m. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Each side is 52 / 4 = 13 m, so the area is 13 x 13 = 169 sq m. Squaring the perimeter gives 2704.

questions.stem: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 10 o'clock?
questions.explanation: Each hour mark is 360 / 12 = 30 degrees apart. At 10 o'clock the hands are 2 marks apart going the short way (10 to 12): 2 x 30 = 60 degrees. The other way round is 300 degrees; 90 and 120 come from counting 3 or 4 marks instead of 2.

questions.stem: What is the average of 14, 22, 9, 31 and 19?
questions.explanation: The sum is 95 and there are 5 numbers, so the average is 95 / 5 = 19. Dividing by 4 by mistake gives 23.75.

questions.stem: A bottle holds 2 litres 350 ml of juice. How many millilitres is that? Type the number only.
questions.explanation: 1 litre = 1000 ml, so 2 litres 350 ml = 2000 + 350 = 2350 ml.

questions.stem: Activities in a mathematics laboratory mainly help children
questions.explanation: A maths lab lets children handle materials, measure, test and find patterns for themselves, so concepts grow from their own activity.

questions.stem: In the analytic method of solving a problem, the reasoning moves from
questions.explanation: Analysis starts from what is to be found and works back to what is given. Synthesis goes the other way, from the known facts to the unknown result.

questions.stem: Which gives a teacher the best picture of how a child understands subtraction?
options: The number of sums she gets right on a test
How quickly she finishes the sheet
The child explaining her steps aloud
questions.explanation: Hearing a child explain her method shows her thinking and reveals any misconception. A score or a speed only shows the end result.

questions.stem: According to George Polya, the first step in solving a problem is to
questions.explanation: Polya's four steps are understand the problem, devise a plan, carry out the plan and look back. Children often skip the first step and go straight to calculating.

questions.stem: Which flower is the state flower of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Palash (flame of the forest), whose orange flowers were used to make Holi colours, is Uttar Pradesh's state flower. The lotus is India's national flower.

questions.stem: Amarbel (Cuscuta) has no green leaves and takes its food from the plant it grows on. Such a plant is a
questions.explanation: A parasite lives on another living thing and takes food from it. Amarbel wraps round its host and draws food through special roots.

questions.stem: Which of these animals sheds its old skin from time to time?
questions.explanation: Snakes shed their outer skin as they grow, often leaving the whole skin in one piece. This is called moulting.

questions.stem: Which organ helps us keep our balance?
questions.explanation: The inner ear has fluid-filled canals that sense the movement of the head and help us keep our balance, besides helping us hear.

questions.stem: Which gas is there more of in the air we breathe out than in the air we breathe in?
questions.explanation: Our body uses oxygen and produces carbon dioxide, so breathed-out air has more carbon dioxide and less oxygen than breathed-in air.

questions.stem: A house built with bricks, cement and iron rods, which stands strong for many years, is called a
questions.explanation: A pucca house is made of strong, lasting materials such as bricks, cement, stone and iron. A kutcha house is built of mud, straw, bamboo or wood and needs repair after heavy rain.

questions.stem: Rani stands facing the rising sun. Which direction is on her left?
questions.explanation: The sun rises in the east, so she faces east. With east in front, north is on the left and south on the right.

questions.stem: Coir, used to make ropes and doormats, comes from
options: the stem of the jute plant
questions.explanation: Coir is the tough fibre in the outer husk of the coconut, worked mostly in Kerala and the other coastal states. Jute fibre comes from the stem of the jute plant.

questions.stem: Children act out a family buying tickets and boarding a train. In EVS, this role play mainly helps them
options: learn the rules of English grammar
questions.explanation: Role play lets children live through a situation, connect it with their own experience and talk about it, which deepens understanding of the theme.

questions.stem: A teacher in a village school brings leaves, grains and seeds from nearby fields into the EVS class. This mainly
options: replaces all visits to the field
questions.explanation: EVS starts from the child's own environment. Real local materials make the lesson familiar and meaningful.

questions.stem: An EVS worksheet made up only of fill-in-the-blanks from the textbook mainly tests
questions.explanation: Filling blanks from the book checks whether facts are remembered. It says little about observation, reasoning or expression.

questions.stem: NCERT's learning outcomes for EVS are statements of
options: how many chapters must be taught in a year
what a child should be able to do
how marks are to be divided
questions.explanation: Learning outcomes describe, class by class, what a child should be able to do (for example 'explains the functions of family members'), so teachers can plan and assess.

questions.stem: A child sees a clay ball rolled into a sausage but cannot imagine rolling it back into a ball. Piaget called this limitation
questions.explanation: Irreversibility is the inability to mentally undo an action, a feature of preoperational thought. Centration is focusing on only one feature, a related but different limit.

questions.stem: According to Erikson, children of about 3 to 6 years face the conflict of
questions.explanation: In the preschool years children try out plans and play roles; encouragement builds initiative and harsh criticism builds guilt. Autonomy versus shame and doubt comes before it, in the toddler years.

questions.stem: Kohlberg's theory of moral development has how many levels?
questions.explanation: Kohlberg described three levels (preconventional, conventional and postconventional), each with two stages, so six stages in all. Six is the number of stages, not levels.

questions.stem: A child avoids eye contact, finds it hard to join in conversation and becomes upset when the daily routine changes. These are common signs of
questions.explanation: Difficulty with social communication together with a strong need for routine and repetitive behaviour are core features of autism spectrum disorder. Many autistic children have average or high intelligence.

questions.stem: A teacher asks, 'How many different uses can you think of for an empty bottle?' This question mainly develops
questions.explanation: Divergent thinking produces many possible answers to an open question and is linked with creativity. Convergent thinking narrows down to one correct answer.

questions.stem: Which psychologist claimed he could train any healthy infant to become a doctor or a thief, depending only on the environment?
questions.explanation: Watson, the founder of behaviourism, made this famous claim for the power of environment. Galton, by contrast, stressed heredity, and Gesell stressed maturation.

questions.stem: A child learns about numbers through pictures and diagrams rather than objects or symbols. In Bruner's terms, this is the
questions.explanation: Bruner described three modes of representation: enactive (through action and objects), iconic (through images) and symbolic (through words and numerals).

questions.stem: A reading book shows only girls cooking and only boys playing cricket. This mainly reinforces
questions.explanation: Showing each activity only with one gender teaches children that some work and play belong to boys and some to girls. Teachers should choose or add material that shows everyone doing everything.

questions.stem: Letting a gifted child move through the syllabus faster than usual, for example by joining a higher class early, is called
questions.explanation: Acceleration speeds up a gifted child's progress, by early entry or by skipping a class. Enrichment keeps the child with the class but adds depth and breadth, and remediation helps children who are behind.

questions.stem: Who held that language and social interaction drive a child's cognitive development?
questions.explanation: Vygotsky saw thought developing through social interaction and language. Piaget held that thinking develops first and language reflects it.

questions.stem: A teacher begins a lesson on fractions by asking how a roti is shared equally among four people at home. She is following the maxim
questions.explanation: Starting from what children already know (sharing a roti) and moving to the new idea (fractions) is the maxim 'from known to unknown'. The other sound maxims run from concrete to abstract and from simple to complex, the reverse of two of the distractors.

questions.stem: Basic education (Nai Talim), in which children learn through a productive craft, was proposed by
questions.explanation: Gandhi put forward Nai Talim in 1937, with learning built around crafts such as spinning. Gijubhai Badheka is known for child-centred pre-primary education in Gujarat.

questions.stem: Self-correcting teaching apparatus and a prepared environment are features of the method of
questions.explanation: Montessori designed didactic apparatus that lets a child see and correct her own mistakes, in a carefully prepared classroom. Froebel founded the kindergarten and its gifts.

questions.stem: A child who is tired and hungry does not respond to a lesson however well it is taught. Thorndike would explain this by his law of
questions.explanation: The law of readiness says learning goes well when the learner is prepared, physically and mentally, to act. A tired, hungry child is not ready.

questions.stem: The foundational stage in NEP 2020's 5+3+3+4 structure covers children of ages
questions.explanation: The foundational stage is five years: three of pre-school or anganwadi (ages 3 to 6) and Classes 1 and 2 (ages 6 to 8). The preparatory stage then covers Classes 3 to 5.

questions.stem: At the top of Maslow's hierarchy of needs is the need for
questions.explanation: Maslow placed self-actualisation, becoming all one can be, at the top, above esteem, love and belonging, safety and physiological needs.

questions.stem: According to George Miller, short-term memory holds about how many items at a time?
questions.explanation: Miller's 'magical number seven, plus or minus two' describes the limited capacity of short-term memory. Grouping items into chunks helps children hold more.

questions.stem: Which question is most likely to make Class 5 children think rather than recall?
options: What is the name of this river?
Why do you think the river flooded?
In which year did the river flood?
Which town is on the bank of the river?
questions.explanation: An open 'why' question asks children to reason and explain. The others have one remembered answer.

questions.stem: Short dated notes a teacher writes about significant things a child said or did are called
questions.explanation: Anecdotal records are brief factual notes of meaningful incidents, gathered over time to understand a child. A rating scale scores fixed qualities on a scale.

questions.stem: Under the RTE Act, at least three-fourths of the members of a School Management Committee must be
questions.explanation: Section 21 of the RTE Act says at least three-fourths of the SMC must be parents or guardians of pupils, with proportionate representation for disadvantaged groups and half the members women.

questions.stem: गर्मियों की दोपहर में नीम की छाया में कौन सुस्ताते हैं?
questions.explanation: The first paragraph says रिक्शेवाले सुस्ताते हैं in its shade, while children play गिल्ली-डंडा there.

questions.stem: नगर निगम पेड़ को क्यों काटना चाहता था?
options: पेड़ के पूरी तरह सूख जाने से
questions.explanation: The passage says the corporation decided to cut it सड़क चौड़ी करने के लिए. The platform was built later, after the tree was saved.

questions.stem: नीम का पेड़ किस प्रकार बचा?
questions.explanation: When the residents asked for the map to be checked again, it turned out that bending the road slightly would save the tree.

questions.stem: गद्यांश में आए शब्द "निर्णय" का पर्यायवाची शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: निर्णय means a decision, the same as फ़ैसला. निवेदन is a request, which the residents made.

questions.stem: "सरस" का विलोम शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: स + रस (with flavour or charm) is opposed by नीरस (without it). सरल means simple, and रसिक means a person of taste.

questions.stem: "स्वागत" शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
questions.explanation: सु (good) + आगत (arrival): उ + आ = वा, which is यण संधि. स्व + आगत is the common wrong split; the word means a good welcome, not one's own arrival.

questions.stem: "अनुशासन" शब्द में कौन-सा उपसर्ग है?
questions.explanation: अनु + शासन = अनुशासन. शासन is the root word, and अन is a different prefix meaning not.

questions.stem: "साकेत" महाकाव्य के रचयिता कौन हैं?
questions.explanation: साकेत, the epic that retells the Ramayana with Lakshman's wife उर्मिला at its centre, is by Maithilisharan Gupt, honoured as राष्ट्रकवि. Jaishankar Prasad wrote कामायनी, and Dinkar wrote कुरुक्षेत्र and रश्मिरथी.

questions.stem: निदानात्मक परीक्षण का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है?
questions.explanation: A diagnostic test finds the exact difficulty, for example confusing two मात्राएँ, so that remedial teaching can follow. Grading and promotion are the work of summative assessment.

questions.stem: सस्वर वाचन से मुख्य रूप से क्या विकसित होता है?
options: तेज़ गति से मौन पठन की क्षमता
questions.explanation: Reading aloud trains clear pronunciation, pauses and rhythm. Speed and comprehension are the strengths of silent reading.

questions.stem: बच्चों की वर्तनी संबंधी अशुद्धियाँ दूर करने का सबसे अच्छा उपाय क्या है?
options: शब्दों को वाक्यों में लिखने का अभ्यास
हर गलत शब्द को बीस-बीस बार लिखवाना
questions.explanation: Using a word in meaningful sentences fixes its spelling better than mechanical copying. Writing a word twenty times is tiring and soon forgotten.

questions.stem: भाषा का मूल और पहला रूप कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: Every language is spoken before it is written, and children speak long before they can write. Writing is a later way of recording speech.

questions.stem: बच्चों का शब्द भंडार बढ़ाने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त उपाय क्या है?
questions.explanation: Children pick up new words when they meet them in stories and play with them in word games. Memorising dictionary pages or word lists gives words without use.

questions.stem: कक्षा में अख़बार, पोस्टर, लेबल और विज्ञापन लगाने से बच्चों को क्या मिलता है?
questions.explanation: A print-rich environment surrounds children with real written language so they meet words in use every day, which supports early reading.

questions.stem: कक्षा में नाटक और अभिनय करवाने से मुख्य रूप से क्या विकसित होता है?
options: व्याकरण के नियमों का गहरा ज्ञान
questions.explanation: Drama gets children to speak with feeling in front of others, so oral expression and confidence grow. It does little for handwriting or grammar rules.

questions.stem: कक्षा का एक बच्चा बोलते समय हकलाता है। शिक्षक को क्या करना चाहिए?
options: उसे धीरे बोलने के लिए डाँटना
उसे मौखिक कार्य से छूट देना
उसके वाक्य जल्दी से पूरे कर देना
धैर्य से सुनना और बोलने के अवसर देना
questions.explanation: A child who stammers needs time and calm listeners. Finishing his sentences, excusing him from speaking or scolding him all add pressure and make the stammer worse.

questions.stem: भाषा के आकलन में खुले प्रश्न (जिनका एक उत्तर न हो) क्यों उपयोगी हैं?
options: रटी हुई बातें जाँचने के लिए
एक जैसे उत्तर पाने के लिए
बच्चे की अपनी सोच जानने के लिए
questions.explanation: Open questions let each child answer in her own words, so the teacher sees how she thinks and uses language. Closed questions mainly test recall.

questions.stem: पढ़ना सिखाने की ध्वनि विधि में बच्चे क्या करते हैं?
options: शब्दों को आकार से याद करते हैं
वर्णों की ध्वनियाँ जोड़कर शब्द पढ़ते हैं
पूरा वाक्य चित्र से पहचानते हैं
questions.explanation: In the phonic (ध्वनि) method children learn the sound of each letter and blend them: क + म + ल = कमल. Recognising whole words by shape is the look-and-say method.

questions.stem: What did Rahim make his kites from?
questions.explanation: The passage says he made kites 'from tissue paper and thin strips of bamboo'.

questions.stem: Why did Rahim not take the falling kite from the boy?
options: He was too busy making other kites
He wanted the boy to learn himself
He thought the kite was broken
He did not like the boy
questions.explanation: Instead of fixing it for him, Rahim made the boy feel the wind and face it, so the boy could succeed on his own.

questions.stem: Which lesson does Rahim's saying, 'It climbs against it', best teach?
questions.explanation: A kite rises by facing the wind, and the saying suggests that facing difficulties, not avoiding them, lifts us up.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: "The parent-teacher meeting is ___ Saturday."
questions.explanation: Days of the week take 'on'. 'In' goes with months and years, and 'at' with clock times.

questions.stem: The idiom 'to bell the cat' means
options: to make a lot of noise
to take on a risky task
questions.explanation: From the fable of the mice who agree a bell on the cat would warn them, but none dares tie it on: 'to bell the cat' is to do the dangerous job everyone else avoids.

questions.stem: A new learner listens to English for weeks before she starts speaking it. This stage is called the
questions.explanation: In second language acquisition many children go through a silent period, taking in the language before they speak. It is normal and should not be forced.

questions.stem: Three school bells ring every 10, 12 and 16 minutes. If they ring together at 9:00, after how many minutes will they next ring together?
questions.explanation: They ring together again after the LCM of 10, 12 and 16: 10 = 2 x 5, 12 = 2 x 2 x 3 and 16 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2, so the LCM is 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 = 240. 60 and 80 are the LCMs of only two of the bells, and 480 is a common multiple but not the least.

questions.stem: What is the sum of all the even numbers from 2 to 20?
questions.explanation: There are 10 even numbers from 2 to 20 and they pair up as 2 + 20 = 22, five times: 5 x 22 = 110. 100 is the sum of the odd numbers 1 to 19, 90 stops at 18, and 55 is the sum of 1 to 10.

questions.stem: A box is 6 cm long, 4 cm wide and 3 cm high. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume = length x breadth x height = 6 x 4 x 3 = 72 cubic cm. 108 is the surface area in square cm, and 13 is the sum of the sides.

questions.stem: How is 4,07,05,060 read in the Indian system?
options: Four crore seven lakh fifty thousand sixty
Four crore seven lakh five thousand sixty
Four crore seventy lakh five thousand sixty
Forty crore seven lakh five thousand six
questions.explanation: Group from the right as crore, lakh, thousand, hundreds: 4 | 07 | 05 | 060 is four crore, seven lakh, five thousand and sixty.

questions.stem: What comes next: 2, 6, 14, 30, ...?
questions.explanation: Each term is double the one before plus 2: 30 x 2 + 2 = 62. Doubling only gives 60, and adding the next gap of 16 gives 46.

questions.stem: A triangle whose three sides are all of different lengths is called
questions.explanation: Scalene triangles have no equal sides. Isosceles have two equal sides and equilateral three.

questions.stem: How many packets of 250 g each can be filled from 6 kg of sugar? Type the number only.
questions.explanation: 6 kg = 6000 g, and 6000 / 250 = 24 packets.

questions.stem: What is 45% of 380?
questions.explanation: 45% of 380 = 45 / 100 x 380 = 171. Misplacing the decimal point gives 17.1 or 1710.

questions.stem: The heuristic method, in which children find things out for themselves like a researcher, was put forward by
questions.explanation: Armstrong developed the heuristic method for science and mathematics. Kilpatrick is linked with the project method and Froebel with the kindergarten.

questions.stem: The project method, in which children solve a real problem as a purposeful activity, is linked with
questions.explanation: Kilpatrick, a student of John Dewey, developed the project method, for example planning and costing a class picnic.

questions.stem: Fraction strips of the same length cut into halves, thirds and quarters are most useful for
questions.explanation: Laying strips side by side shows, for example, that 1/3 is smaller than 1/2 even though 3 is bigger than 2.

questions.stem: Base-ten blocks (ones, rods and flats) are most useful for teaching
questions.explanation: Ten ones can be swapped for a rod and ten rods for a flat, so children see carrying and borrowing as real exchanges.

questions.stem: When children only memorise times tables without understanding, the main problem is that they
options: cannot apply them in new situations
recite them too slowly in the class test
questions.explanation: Rote memory gives answers to the table itself but not the meaning of multiplication, so children struggle to use it in word problems or new contexts.

questions.stem: In Bruner's spiral curriculum, a topic such as fractions is
options: taught once, completely, in one class
left until the child is twelve
revisited at greater depth each year
questions.explanation: Bruner argued that any subject can be taught in some honest form at any age and then returned to, more deeply, as the child grows.

questions.stem: A Class 2 child keeps writing 5 < 3. The most useful first step for the teacher is to
options: move on and come back next year
compare real groups of objects with her
make her copy the two symbols many times
tell her the rule more loudly
questions.explanation: Comparing a group of 5 objects with a group of 3 lets the child see which is more, and the symbol can then be linked to what she sees.

questions.stem: Before working out 49 x 21, a teacher asks children to guess roughly what the answer will be. This develops
questions.explanation: Estimating first (about 50 x 20 = 1000) builds number sense and helps children spot answers that cannot be right.

questions.stem: The main weakness of the lecture method in primary mathematics is that children
options: learn too many concepts at once
questions.explanation: In a lecture the teacher talks and the children listen, so they do not handle, try or explain the ideas themselves.

questions.stem: The play-way approach to early learning, with gifts and occupations for young children, comes from
questions.explanation: Froebel, the founder of the kindergarten, believed young children learn best through play and designed his 'gifts' (balls, blocks, shapes) for it.

questions.stem: The seeds of which plant are spread mainly by the wind?
questions.explanation: Cotton seeds are covered in light hairs that the wind carries far. The coconut floats on water, and mango seeds are spread when animals eat the fruit.

questions.stem: Animals such as the owl that are active at night are called
questions.explanation: Nocturnal animals rest by day and hunt or feed at night. Migratory animals travel between places with the seasons.

questions.stem: A balanced diet is one that has
options: more fat and less protein than usual
all nutrients in the right amounts
questions.explanation: A balanced diet gives carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, roughage and water in the right proportions for growth and health.

questions.stem: What is the right first aid for a small burn on the hand?
options: Rub butter or oil on it
Hold it under cool running water
Cover it with toothpaste at once
questions.explanation: Cool running water for several minutes takes heat out of the skin and eases the pain. Butter, oil and toothpaste trap heat and can cause infection.

questions.stem: The Chipko movement was started by villagers to
questions.explanation: In the Chipko movement of the 1970s, villagers in the hills of Uttarakhand (then part of Uttar Pradesh) hugged trees to stop them being felled.

questions.stem: The inside of a box-type solar cooker is painted black because black surfaces
options: absorb more of the sun's heat
questions.explanation: Dark, dull surfaces absorb most of the sunlight falling on them and turn it into heat, while white or shiny surfaces reflect it. The glass lid then keeps that heat inside the box.

questions.stem: Sugarcane, grown widely in western Uttar Pradesh, is crushed in mills mainly to make
questions.explanation: Juice pressed from sugarcane is boiled into gur (jaggery) in villages and refined into sugar in mills. Uttar Pradesh grows more sugarcane than any other state.

questions.stem: Meena's mother's brother is Meena's
questions.explanation: A mother's brother is mama. A father's younger brother is chacha, a mother's sister's husband is mausa, and a father's sister's husband is fufa.

questions.stem: Using a story to begin an EVS lesson on animals mainly
questions.explanation: Stories capture young children's attention and give them a context for the concept. They work best followed by observation and discussion.

questions.stem: In EVS, the 'environment' of a child includes
options: only plants and animals around us
questions.explanation: EVS treats the environment as both natural (plants, animals, water, air) and social (family, community, work, festivals).

questions.stem: Which picture in an EVS lesson on work best supports gender equality?
options: A mother driving and a father cooking
Only women carrying water from the well
questions.explanation: Showing people doing work regardless of gender challenges stereotypes about 'men's work' and 'women's work'.

questions.stem: To show that seeds need water to sprout, children keep one dish of seeds dry and another moist, with the same seeds, soil and place. Why keep everything else the same?
options: So that the dishes look neat
So the teacher can save time
questions.explanation: In a fair test only the factor being studied changes. If the dishes also differed in seeds, soil or light, children could not tell what caused the difference in sprouting.

questions.stem: Class 5 is going on a field visit to a pond. One child uses a wheelchair. The teacher should
options: plan a route every child can use
let the child skip the activity
leave the child at school that day
questions.explanation: Inclusion means planning activities so every child takes part. A reachable route and spot let the whole class learn together.

questions.stem: Many questions in NCERT EVS books, such as 'What do you like to eat at home?', have no single right answer because they
questions.explanation: Such questions invite children to share their own experience and views, so learning begins from what they already know.

questions.stem: In EVS teaching, the textbook should be treated as
questions.explanation: NCF 2005 asks teachers to go beyond the textbook, using the surroundings, people, newspapers and activities as resources.

questions.stem: A teacher gives children a tub of water and objects, and asks them to find out which ones float. This is
questions.explanation: Children predict, try and find out for themselves, the core of inquiry-based learning.

questions.stem: Asking children to say what they learned and what they found hard after an EVS project mainly helps them
questions.explanation: Self-assessment builds the habit of reflection, so children notice their own progress and gaps.

questions.stem: The best way to begin map work in Class 4 is to have children
options: draw a map of their own classroom
questions.explanation: Map skills start from the near and known: drawing the classroom or home shows them what a map is before moving to larger areas.
